question: Which film will win the Étoile d’Or at the 2026 Marrakech International Film Festival?

calls.reasoning: Reference class: Marrakech Étoile d'Or winners since the first/second-feature format (2018-2025: Joy, Mosaic Portrait, Snow and the Bear, Mother of All Lies, Happy Holidays, Promised Sky). These were usually films with a prize or strong slot at Cannes or Venice, and the last three were Arab/Maghreb films. Ben'imana (Cannes Caméra d'Or + FIPRESCI) leads, helped by a jury that includes Ramata-Toulaye Sy, Kaouther Ben Hania and Saïd Hamich. Next come House of the Wind (Venice Orizzonti special jury prize + debut award) and Congo Boy (UCR best actor). The World Before (TIFF Platform, San Sebastián mention), Marie Madeleine (Cannes Première; actress-led jury), Sad Girlz (Berlin Generation Crystal Bear), Our Share of Sand (Venice Critics' Week audience award) and Jo (Orizzonti best director) form the middle tier. Chronicles from the Siege was withdrawn by its producer around Nov 18, so ~0. 'Other' is fat: 5 unlisted films, including Arab-world titles (Alkebulan, Furies, Cairo Shadows, Waves of Silence) that fit the recent winner pattern, plus a small chance of a shared award. No prediction market or bookmaker found.

calls.reasoning: Thirteen films remain in competition after the Algerian rights-holder withdrew Chronicles from the Siege on the eve of the festival. Recent Étoile d'Or winners skew toward MENA films (Iran 2022, Morocco 2023, Palestine 2024, Tunisia 2025). Those entries — Alkebulan (Moroccan world premiere, Atlas-backed), Cairo Shadows, Waves of Silence and Furies — all fall under Other, together with Eklipse and a ~2% chance of a shared award or no winner. Ben'Imana has the strongest pedigree (Caméra d'Or, FIPRESCI) and an African-leaning jury (Ben Hania, Sy, Hamich), but Marrakech juries often skip the most decorated film. Jo (Venice Orizzonti director, Thessaloniki Golden Alexander), Congo Boy, Sad Girlz, Our Share of Sand, The World Before and Marie Madeleine are close to evenly matched. No human market found on Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or bookmakers.

Recent winners (2023 Mother of All Lies, 2024 Happy Holidays, 2025 Promised Sky) skew toward films with Cannes Un Certain Regard or Venice Orizzonti pedigree and an Arab or African subject, often Atlas Workshops alumni. Chronicles from the Siege, the Berlinale best-first-feature winner and the natural MENA favourite, was withdrawn by its Algerian producer over Morocco-Israel ties, so it is near zero. Ben'Imana (Caméra d'Or plus FIPRESCI, Rwandan genocide-reparation story, Atlas alumnus) is the pedigree favourite; Lentzou's Venice and Thessaloniki winner is next. Congo Boy, Marie Madeleine and House of the Wind fit the African-cinema lean. 'Other' covers Furies, Cairo Shadows (Atlas-backed world premiere), Eklipse, Alkebulan, Waves of Silence and a shared award. No betting market found on Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or bookmakers.
